summary: The v70 five-arrow stack reaches invent.c:adjust_split through the queued item-action path. The first mismatch at step 101 is a ReferenceError: js/invent.js uses GC_ECHOFIRST and GC_CONDHIST in its multi-item get_count call without importing either constant. C defines both flags in hack.h (values 4 and 2); js/const.js already exports them. The prefix matches through step 100, including 2203 RNG calls. The fix is to import both existing flags and test the >2 stack path through itemactions and rhack.

source.branch: adjust_split: when the selected object has quantity greater than two, C reads the first digit with yn_function and calls get_count with GC_ECHOFIRST|GC_CONDHIST before validating the amount and splitting the object.

evidence: challenges/manifests/v70.json identifies invent.c:adjust_split as the C owner and records the expected five-arrow split: the input asks “Split off how many?”, enters 2, and selects destination b.

challenges/evaluations/admission-f5371e6adf39dfbf6b3bc839f5d6d96195f0536f-v70.json records the first mismatch at segment 0, step 101, key 2: ReferenceError GC_ECHOFIRST is not defined. The C prefix matches 101 screens and 2203 RNG calls before that boundary.

nethack-c/upstream/src/invent.c:5008-5065 calls get_count with GC_ECHOFIRST|GC_CONDHIST for quantity greater than two; hack.h:1386-1388 defines those values as 4 and 2. js/const.js already exports both values.
js/invent.js:5570-5584 uses both constants but imports neither. js/cmd.js already imports and passes the same flags to its get_count implementation.

The production caller is iactions.c:itemactions_pushkeys (IA_ADJUST_STACK queues adjust_split) followed by cmd.c:rhack invoking the queued function pointer. js/iactions.js and js/cmd.js already implement that same queue and dispatch path.

scripts/cmd.test.mjs:3858 covers this item-action dispatch only for quantity two; that branch skips get_count. Extend it with a quantity-five stack and keys 2, space, and a destination letter to cover the failing branch and C message/split order.
The admitted v70 crosswalk distinguishes this failure from v47 two-egg splitting (which defaults to one and bypasses get_count) and v69 #adjust (which uses doorganize/getobj).
